calibration.note: Per-customer instances here (20-30 payments, 15-22 invoices, 10 customers per scenario) are sized specifically so exact solving is impractical: a bitmask/subset dynamic-programming solver (the textbook approach for subset-sum-family problems) was measured directly on this scenario family and takes 17s at n=15 payments and exceeds 120s (did not finish) at n=18 -- these scenarios use n=20-30, well past that threshold. Swept across 15 independently generated scenarios (not just this one): six adversarial greedy probes land at 16.1%-22.6% of total payment value uncleared with zero exceptions, while two structurally independent search algorithms (simulated annealing over single reassignments; GRASP-style randomized construction with large-neighborhood-search repair) both converge to 3.7%-5.7% when properly tuned (many iterations/restarts) -- a robust 3.4x-5.4x gap on every scenario tried. Effort sensitivity was also measured directly on this held-out scenario: a single annealing pass with only 200-1500 iterations (a quick, minimally-tuned first attempt) lands at 10.0%-18.0%, only reaching the bar's territory at 3000+ iterations (7.1%) -- genuine iterative refinement against measured results is required, a single naive implementation is not sufficient. The pass bar sits between the quick-attempt range and the tuned reference, requiring real experimentation without requiring exact optimality (which is not computationally reachable at this scale).
